why: All three checks pass. (1) The quoted sentence exists verbatim at hooks.md:2472 of the live fetch, with the field table at :2474-2477 defining `file_path` as the absolute path and `event` as `change`|`add`|`unlink`, plus a JSON example at :2479-2487. (2) packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.ts:228-232 emits `{ hook_event_name: 'FileChanged', change_kind: toolName, ...(path ? { path } : {}) }`, and the cited hook-command.ts:646 is inside `hookCommandStdinPayload` (:641-651), which spreads `...input` and adds only `hook_event_name` and `cwd` — no key rewriting. The shape is additionally frozen by lifecycle-bridge.test.ts:90. (3) No layer up or down rescues it: `grep -ran change_kind packages apps` returns only lifecycle-bridge, its test, types.ts:805 and the frozen contract row types.ts:73; the emit chain (lifecycleEventSink -> index.ts:1969 `automation_event` -> pi-agent.ts:2325 -> emitAutomationEvent -> dispatchAutomationAgentEvent) renames nothing; and there is no sibling emitter — claude-agent.ts never emits FileChanged, and the other files naming it only register the event name. The only code that knows the documented spelling is the matcher helper `changedFileBasename` (utils.ts:150-154, `input.file_path ?? input.path`), which accepts a key nothing produces. Not one of the nine owner decisions in inert-worklist.md §3 (seatbelt wildcard, availableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries), and not a branding/gateway/subscription product difference. correctedState: Confirmed, with three refinements that strengthen it. (a) The emitter never produces `file_path` or `event`, but the fork is not wholly ignorant of the documented key: the matcher helper `changedFileBasename` (packages/shared/src/automations/utils.ts:150-154) reads `input.file_path ?? input.path`. It is read-side only, so `jq -r .file_path` on stdin still yields null — the claimed consequence holds. (b) The divergence is wider than field names: this fork's FileChanged is not a disk-watcher event at all. It fires on successful completion of a file-mutating TOOL (`FILE_MUTATING_TOOLS = write|edit|replace_in_file|multi_edit`, lifecycle-bridge.ts:52), so there is no `add`/`unlink` distinction available (a deletion never fires it), no watch list built from the matcher, and no `watchPaths` output honoured. (c) `path` is whatever the tool argument carried (`mutatedPath` reads `path ?? file_path ?? filePath`, lifecycle-bridge.ts:85-89), so it is not guaranteed absolute as the doc requires, and it is omitted entirely when the tool_execution_start/end correlation captured nothing.
